title: Multi-Container Pod Patterns

header.html: Understand multi-container Pod design patterns (e.g. sidecar, init and others)

toc.title: Why more than one container in a Pod

html:
1Why more than one container in a Pod

All containers of a Pod run on the same node and share two things: the network (one IP address, localhost reaches the other containers) and the volumes you mount into them. They do not share the file system of the image or the process list by default. Put two containers in one Pod only when they must work as one unit and be scheduled, scaled and restarted together.

Pattern What the extra container does Example
Init container runs to completion before the main containers start wait for a Service, download a file, set permissions
Sidecar runs next to the main container for its whole life ship logs, refresh a certificate, sync content
Ambassador a proxy that the main container talks to on localhost connect to a database, hiding sharding or credentials
Adapter converts the main container's output to another format turn app metrics into the format a monitoring system reads

Ambassador and adapter are designs, not special Kubernetes fields: both are ordinary extra containers in spec.containers.

2Init containers

spec.initContainers run one after another, each to completion, before the main containers start. If one fails, the kubelet restarts it (with restartPolicy Always or OnFailure) and the main containers do not start. The Pod shows Init:0/1, Init:1/2, Init:Error or Init:CrashLoopBackOff until they finish.

spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: wait-backend
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "until wget -q -T2 -O /dev/null http://backend; do sleep 2; done"]
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:alpine
  • They can use a different image from the app (tools the app image does not have).
  • They share volumes with the main containers: an init container writes a file to an emptyDir, the app reads it.
  • Their resources count differently: the Pod's effective request is the larger of the biggest init container and the sum of the app containers.
  • A Pod stuck in Init:0/1: read the init container's log, k logs <pod> -c <init-name>, and k describe pod.

3Sidecars and shared volumes

The classic sidecar shares an emptyDir with the main container. The app writes a log file, the sidecar reads it:

containers:
- name: app
  image: busybox:1.36
  command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do date >> /var/log/app/app.log; sleep 2; done"]
  volumeMounts: [{name: logs, mountPath: /var/log/app}]
- name: tailer
  image: busybox:1.36
  command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /var/log/app/app.log"]
  volumeMounts: [{name: logs, mountPath: /var/log/app}]
volumes:
- name: logs
  emptyDir: {}

k logs weblog -c tailer reads one container; with several containers you must give -c, or use --all-containers. k exec -it weblog -c app -- sh enters one. A Pod's containers cannot be added to a running Pod: edit the manifest and recreate (k replace --force -f).

Shared network. Containers in a Pod listen on the same ports: two containers that both bind port 80 clash. The other containers reach a web server in the Pod at http://localhost:80.

4Native sidecar containers

A sidecar declared as a normal container has two problems: it may start after the main container, and in a Job it never stops, so the Job never completes. Kubernetes solves this with native sidecars: put the sidecar in initContainers and set restartPolicy: Always on that one container.

spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  initContainers:
  - name: tail
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    restartPolicy: Always      # this makes it a native sidecar
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo report finished"]
Init container Native sidecar Regular container
Starts before the main containers, in order before the main containers, in order with the main containers
Keeps running no, must finish yes, restarted if it exits yes
Stopped when the main containers end n/a yes, after them n/a
Blocks a Job from completing no no yes

A native sidecar can have its own probes (a startup probe tells the kubelet when the sidecar is ready, so the main container starts after it).

5How to choose

  • It must finish before the app starts: init container.
  • It runs for the app's whole life and shares files or the network: sidecar (a native sidecar in a Job).
  • The app should talk to a local proxy: ambassador.
  • Output must change format for a consumer: adapter.
  • It could run and scale alone: a separate Pod or Deployment, not the same Pod.
Exam tip

. In a task that says "add a container to the Pod", the Pod must be recreated: k get pod x -o yaml > x.yaml, edit, k replace --force -f x.yaml. In a Deployment you can edit in place (k edit deployment), and the Pods are replaced for you.

Exam tip

. Init container problems show in the Pod status first: Init:0/1. Always read k logs <pod> -c <init-container> before changing anything.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m03 -->

Lab 3.1: sidecar log tailer

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-01-sidecar-log-tailer)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace mc, the Pod weblog (manifest ~/work/weblog.yaml) has one container app that appends lines to /var/log/app/app.log on the emptyDir volume logs. Add a sidecar container named tailer with the image busybox:1.36 that runs tail -F /var/log/app/app.log and mounts the same volume at the same path, so that kubectl logs weblog -c tailer shows the log lines. A running Pod cannot gain a container, so recreate the Pod and wait until both containers are Running.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n mc delete pod weblog --wait=true
cat > ~/work/weblog.yaml <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: weblog
  namespace: mc
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "i=0; while true; do echo log line $i >> /var/log/app/app.log; i=$((i+1)); sleep 2; done"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: logs, mountPath: /var/log/app}
  - name: tailer
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /var/log/app/app.log"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: logs, mountPath: /var/log/app}
  volumes:
  - name: logs
    emptyDir: {}
Y
kubectl apply -f ~/work/weblog.yaml
kubectl -n mc wait --for=condition=Ready pod/weblog --timeout=120s
sleep 5
kubectl -n mc logs weblog -c tailer

Lab 3.2: init container content

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-02-init-container-content)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace mc, create a Pod named site with one init container content (image busybox:1.36) and one container web (image nginx:alpine). The init container must write the text welcome to ckad to the file index.html on an emptyDir volume named html; the web container mounts that volume at /usr/share/nginx/html. When the Pod is Ready, requesting it over HTTP must return welcome to ckad.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n mc apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: site
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: content
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo welcome to ckad > /data/index.html"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: html, mountPath: /data}
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:alpine
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: html, mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html}
  volumes:
  - name: html
    emptyDir: {}
Y
kubectl -n mc wait --for=condition=Ready pod/site --timeout=120s

Lab 3.3: init waits for service

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-03-init-waits-for-service)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace mc, the Pods of the Deployment web are stuck in Init:0/1: their init container waits until http://backend answers. The Deployment backend is running. Without changing the Deployment web, make the Pods of web start and become Ready (2 of 2).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n mc describe pod -l app=web | grep -A3 "Init Containers"
kubectl -n mc logs deploy/web -c wait-backend --tail=3
kubectl -n mc get svc
kubectl -n mc expose deployment backend --port=80
kubectl -n mc rollout status deployment web --timeout=180s

Lab 3.4: shared localhost

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 5 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-04-shared-localhost)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace mc, create one Pod named pair with two containers: web (image nginx:alpine) and checker (image busybox:1.36). The checker must run sh -c 'while true; do wget -q -O /dev/null http://localhost:80 && echo ok; sleep 3; done', so its log shows ok as long as it can reach the web container over localhost (containers of one Pod share the network). Wait until the Pod is Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n mc apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: pair
spec:
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:alpine
  - name: checker
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do wget -q -O /dev/null http://localhost:80 && echo ok; sleep 3; done"]
Y
kubectl -n mc wait --for=condition=Ready pod/pair --timeout=120s
sleep 6
kubectl -n mc logs pair -c checker

Lab 3.5: native sidecar job

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-05-native-sidecar-job)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace mc, the Job report never completes, because its Pod has a second container tail (a log helper that sleeps forever) next to the main container main. Keep the tail container, but change the Job so that it completes: declare tail as a native sidecar (an init container with restartPolicy: Always). The manifest is in ~/work/report-job.yaml. A Job's Pod template cannot be edited, so delete the Job and create it again from the corrected file; wait until the Job is complete.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n mc delete job report --wait=true
cat > ~/work/report-job.yaml <<'Y'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: report
  namespace: mc
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      initContainers:
      - name: tail
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep", "3600"]
        restartPolicy: Always
      containers:
      - name: main
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo report finished"]
Y
kubectl apply -f ~/work/report-job.yaml
kubectl -n mc wait --for=condition=complete job/report --timeout=180s

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1What do all containers of one Pod share?

Show the answer

The network (one IP address and localhost) and the volumes they mount.

R2When do init containers run?

Show the answer

One after another, to completion, before the main containers start.

R3What does Init:0/1 mean?

Show the answer

The first of the Pod's one init containers has not finished yet.

R4How do you declare a native sidecar?

Show the answer

As an init container with restartPolicy: Always.

R5Why does a normal sidecar stop a Job from completing, and how does a native sidecar fix it?

Show the answer

A normal container that never exits keeps the Pod running; a native sidecar is stopped after the main containers finish.

R6Which flag reads the log of one container in a multi-container Pod?

Show the answer

-c <container> (for example kubectl logs weblog -c tailer).

R7Which pattern lets the main container reach a database through a local proxy?

Show the answer

The ambassador pattern.

R8Can you add a container to a running Pod?

Show the answer

No; recreate the Pod (or edit the Deployment).

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Shared network (localhost) and mounted volumes, not the image file system
Init container initContainers, runs to completion first; status Init:n/m; log with -c
Sidecar extra container in containers, shares an emptyDir
Native sidecar init container with restartPolicy: Always; Jobs can complete
Ambassador / adapter proxy to the outside / converts output; ordinary containers
Add a container recreate the Pod: replace --force
Which container logs -c, exec -c, --all-containers
